questions.question: What happens to the strength of an electromagnet's magnetic field if you increase the number of turns of wire in its coil?
options: It becomes weaker.
It becomes stronger.
It remains exactly the same.
It disappears completely.

questions.question: How does increasing the electric current flowing through the coil affect an electromagnet?
options: It weakens the magnetic field.
It makes the magnetic field stronger.
It reverses the magnetic poles instantly.
It has no effect on the strength of the magnetic field.

questions.question: Why does inserting a soft iron core into the coil of an electromagnet increase its magnetic strength?
options: The core becomes magnetised when the current is turned on.
The core reduces the electric current to a safer level.
The core acts as an electrical insulator to stop short circuits.
The core increases the physical weight of the coil.

questions.question: What is created around a wire when an electric current passes through it?
options: An electrostatic charge only.
A gravitational field.
A magnetic field.
A chemical reaction.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of an electromagnet compared to a permanent magnet?
options: It can be turned on and off with an electric current.
It never requires any energy source to function.
It is always made of non-metallic materials.
Its poles are permanently fixed and can never be reversed.

questions.question: What will happen if you bring the north-seeking pole of one magnet close to the north-seeking pole of another magnet?
options: They will attract each other.
They will repel each other.
They will cancel each other's magnetism out.
They will spin rapidly in clockwise directions.

questions.question: How do magnetic materials behave when placed near the north-seeking and south-seeking poles of a magnet?
options: They are attracted to both poles.
They are attracted to the north pole but repelled by the south pole.
They are repelled by both poles.
They are attracted to the south pole but repelled by the north pole.

questions.question: Which group contains only the three metal elements that are magnetic?
options: Copper, aluminum, and gold.
Iron, cobalt, and nickel.
Silver, platinum, and zinc.
Lead, tin, and iron.

questions.question: Why does a freely suspended magnet's north-seeking pole point towards the Earth's geographic North Pole?
options: Because the Earth has its own magnetic field.
Because of the Earth's rapid rotational force.
Because of gravitational attraction to polar ice.
Because the North Pole has a lower temperature.

questions.question: How does the needle of a plotting compass behave when placed near a magnet?
options: It spins continuously without stopping.
It lines up with the magnetic field of the magnet.
It points directly perpendicular to the magnetic field.
It points away from all magnetic materials.

questions.question: In which direction can a magnetic field line be followed around a magnet?
options: From the south-seeking pole to the north-seeking pole.
From the north-seeking pole to the south-seeking pole.
From the center of the magnet outwards in straight lines only.
From the sides of the magnet to the poles.

questions.question: Which of the following is a true property of magnetic field lines?
options: They cross over each other where the field is strongest.
They are broken, disconnected segments.
They do not cross over and are continuous.
They only exist inside the metal of the magnet.

questions.question: How does an electromagnetic door lock function to unlock a door?
options: It uses an electromagnet to pull a magnetic bolt.
It heats up a metal key until it expands and turns.
It spins a small motor to grind down the lock mechanism.
It sends an electrical shock to melt the latch.

questions.question: What does the electromagnet in an electric bell do immediately after attracting the striker?
options: It reverses its magnetic polarity to push the striker back.
It increases its current to hold the striker in place.
It breaks its own circuit to let the striker spring back.
It melts a small fuse to permanently turn off the bell.

questions.question: What causes the spinning coil (electromagnet) in a motor to rotate when there is a current?
options: Electrostatic charges on the casing attract the coil.
Other magnets around the coil push it round.
The wire physically contracts and expands due to heat.
Gravitational forces pull the coil downwards.

questions.question: Why will an electromagnet made from bare wire fail to work if the adjacent turns are touching?
options: Because the current flows straight through instead of around the coil.
Because bare wire is unable to conduct any electricity.
Because touching wires will cause the metal to melt immediately.
Because bare wire can only produce static electricity.

questions.question: What happens when an electric current flows through a coil of wire rather than a single straight wire?
options: The magnetic field around each loop adds together to make a stronger field.
The magnetic field of each loop cancels out, resulting in no field.
The current stops flowing due to increased resistance in the loops.
The magnetic field is converted entirely into static electrical energy.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the shape of the magnetic field of a bar magnet?
options: It is completely asymmetrical and chaotic.
It is symmetrical.
It only exists at the exact center of the magnet.
It extends in only one direction from the north pole.
